title: Extension by zero of abelian Zariski sheaves is a left adjoint of restriction to an open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme, and $X_{\rm Zar}$, $U_{\rm Zar}$ the small Zariski sites of $X$ and of $U$ [def-sc-zariski-site] (the objects of $U_{\rm Zar}$ are the opens $W\subseteq U$, which are also objects of $X_{\rm Zar}$, and a family of opens of $W$ is a covering of $W$ in $U_{\rm Zar}$ if and only if it is one in $X_{\rm Zar}$). Let $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$, $\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ be the abelian categories of abelian sheaves on these sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For $\mathcal G\in\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ let $\mathcal G|_U\in\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ be the abelian sheaf $W\mapsto\mathcal G(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) with the restriction maps of $\mathcal G$, and for a morphism $\psi$ of $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ let $(\psi|_U)_W=\psi_W$. For $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ let $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ be the presheaf of abelian groups on $X_{\rm Zar}$ with $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V)$ if $V\subseteq U$ and $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)=0$ if $V\not\subseteq U$ ($V\subseteq X$ open), whose restriction map along $V'\subseteq V$ is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ if $V\subseteq U$ (then also $V'\subseteq U$) and $0$ otherwise; a morphism $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ of $\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ gives $j_{p!}\alpha$, equal to $\alpha_V$ for $V\subseteq U$ and to $0$ otherwise. Let $\theta_{\mathcal F}:j_{p!}\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F$ be the sheafification of $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ as a presheaf of abelian groups on the site $X_{\rm Zar}$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and $j_!\alpha:j_!\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F'$ the unique morphism with $j_!\alpha\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha$; $j_!\mathcal F$ is the *extension of $\mathcal F$ by zero*. Then: (1) $\mathcal F\mapsto j_!\mathcal F$, $\alpha\mapsto j_!\alpha$ is an additive functor $j_!:\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})\to\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$; (2) $j_!$ is left adjoint to restriction: for every $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ and every $\mathcal G\in\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ the map $\Hom_{\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})}(j_!\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\to\Hom_{\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G|_U)$, $\psi\mapsto(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U$ (whose component at $W\subseteq U$ is $\psi_W\circ\theta_{\mathcal F,W}:\mathcal F(W)\to\mathcal G(W)$), is bijective, and natural in $\mathcal F$ and in $\mathcal G$.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DI (label lemma-extension-by-zero, line 2058) and Definition 04IX (label definition-localize-ringed-site, line 2019) (4),(5), for the ringed site (X_Zar, Z) (abelian sheaves) and the object U, whose localization X_Zar/U is U_Zar and for which every V has at most one morphism to U, so the presheaf of 03DI is j_{p!}F; the topological form is Sheaves, Lemma 00A5 (label lemma-j-shriek-abelian, literature/stacks-project/sheaves.tex line 4685) part (2), with Definition 00A4 (label definition-j-shriek-structures, line 4612) (1),(2). The proof of 00A5 is omitted and that of 03DI omits the verification that the two constructions are inverse.
